issues.description: FAQ example reads req.stream with explicit content_length, contradicting the change in things_advanced.py to bounded_stream
issues.detail: The example code added to docs/user/faq.rst calls `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`, while the same PR changes things_advanced.py to use `req.bounded_stream.read()` precisely to handle the empty-body-with-nonzero-Content-Length case correctly. The FAQ is teaching readers a different pattern than the example body it accompanies. A literate-programming-grade explanation must be consistent with the code it documents; pick one idiom (bounded_stream is the safer default) and state the invariant: 'we will never read more bytes than the client claimed, and we will not block waiting for bytes that never arrive.'

issues.description: Loop/branch invariant of the FAQ PostTest handler is not stated and the 400 vs 201 distinction is subtle
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post has three branches keyed off content_length and on whether the read returns truthy bytes. The intended invariant is: 'if the client advertises Content-Length > 0 but provides fewer bytes, respond 400; if it provides the advertised bytes, respond 201; if it advertises nothing, respond 200.' That invariant is the whole point of the example and it is not stated in prose. Without it, a reader cannot tell whether `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)` returning falsy is the intended detection mechanism or an accident of the test harness. Add a one-paragraph literate comment above the handler.

issues.description: Test asserts on a contract (400 for empty body with nonzero Content-Length) without naming the invariant under test
issues.detail: tests/test_examples.py adds resp4 expecting 400 when Content-Length=1 and body is empty. The assertion is correct, but the test has no docstring or comment explaining what behavior is being pinned. For a regression test, the value is in the explanation: 'this guards the bounded_stream change; a regression to req.stream.read() would hang or return empty bytes and break this contract.' Two lines of comment would make the test self-documenting and prevent a future maintainer from 'fixing' it by switching back to req.stream.

issues.description: README.rst diff mixes a behavioral change (handle signature reorder) into a cosmetic reformat without explanation
issues.detail: The README example reorders `StorageError.handle(ex, req, resp, params)` to `handle(req, resp, ex, params)`. That is a real API-signature change (Falcon's error handler protocol), buried in a sea of PEP8-style reflows and string-formatting cleanups. The PR description does not mention this. Either the README was wrong before and the fix deserves its own line in the changelog, or it is wrong now. Audit which signature matches the current Falcon error handler contract and state it. Drive-by reformats hide load-bearing edits.

issues.description: Termination/edge cases of bounded_stream.read() with no Content-Length not addressed in the example or docs
issues.detail: Switching from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() in things_advanced.py changes behavior when Content-Length is absent or when chunked transfer encoding is in play. The PR adds no comment in the example file explaining why bounded_stream is preferred and what it guarantees (will not block past the declared body length). A one-line literate comment at the call site would make the example pedagogically honest: the example exists to teach, and silently swapping read sources is the opposite of teaching.

issues.description: FAQ test uses `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` with redundant parens, suggesting `assert` was mistaken for a function call
issues.detail: `assert(expr)` works but reads as a function call and can mask the common pitfall `assert(expr, msg)` which is always true. In a public FAQ that readers will copy, the idiom should be `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`. Small thing, but the FAQ is the canonical reading surface; readability matters more here than in test code.

review.summary: The PR's substantive content is small and reasonable: switch the things_advanced example to bounded_stream and add two POST tests that pin the new behavior (UNDER-AUDITED leaning RIGOROUS at the algorithmic level — the streaming-read invariant is what is being protected, and it is correctly protected by resp4). However, the documentation half of the change is NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT throughout: the FAQ teaches a pattern (req.stream.read(content_length)) that contradicts the example it ships alongside (bounded_stream), no invariant is stated for the three-branch PostTest handler, and the new test has no comment explaining what regression it guards. Separately, the README diff smuggles a real signature change (StorageError.handle argument order) into a cosmetic reflow — that needs to be called out and verified against Falcon's current error-handler contract, not hidden in PEP8 churn. No correctness or complexity concerns at the algorithm level; the audit gaps are all in the explanation layer, which is exactly where this lens cares most.
